text:
maya: Heads-up — I prototyped a TF change to add a graceful spot fallback policy + price hysteresis for GPU pools. posting plan snippet for context.

sam: nice. what's the high-level?

maya: goal: reduce MTTR when spot capacity drops in a region, avoid churn from tiny price blips, and keep latency SLO for short jobs. steps: (1) introduce "fallback_policy" on module gpu_pool, (2) add `price_hysteresis_pct` that gates fallback to on-demand, (3) tag instances so billing/ops can filter fallbacks, (4) exclude certain instance AMIs that show ENA perf regressions.

arjun: quick note — we saw weird networking stalls on older RHEL AMIs causing long pod startup times on g5/rtx pools. excluding bad AMI sounds good.

maya: exact tf fragment I'm proposing:

```hcl
module "gpu_pool" {
  source = "github.com/redwood/infrastructure//modules/gpu_pool"

  instance_types = ["g5.2xlarge", "g5.8xlarge", "a10g.8xlarge"]
  fallback_policy = {
    enabled = true
    target = "on_demand"
    price_hysteresis_pct = 12
    canary_percent = 10
  }

  ami_blacklist = ["ami-0deadbeef1234", "ami-0cafe12345678"]
  tags = merge(var.tags, { "spot_fallback" = "true" })
}
```

liz: can we keep lower-priced preemptible only in non-critical AZs? i.e., don't fallback to spot in primary AZ until hysteresis exceeded?

maya: yes — canary_percent + per-az weight logic in module will route new capacity requests to safety AZs first. plan includes new `az_weights` map.

terraform-bot: plan: 7 to add, 2 to change, 0 to destroy.

terraform-bot: diff shows new iam policy for tag-read and an autoscaling lifecycle hook to drain on interruption:

```
+ resource "aws_autoscaling_lifecycle_hook" "drain_on_interruption" {
+   name = "drain-on-interruption"
+   autoscaling_group_name = module.gpu_asg.name
+   lifecycle_transition = "autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING"
+   notification_target_arn = aws_sns.topic.interrupt_notifications.arn
+ }
```

sam: good — lifecycle hook is critical. how do we test?

maya: propose rollout: 10% canary in us-west-2 first, with an automated smoke job that submits 200 short (<30s) generation requests at p50 latency targets. if cost delta < 6% and error rates stable, promote to 50% then 100% over 24h windows.

arjun: we should also add a quick kernel/ENA probe during bootstrap to detect faulty AMIs and mark them unhealthy via instance tag so scheduler excludes them. simple curl to metadata + dmesg parse.

maya: adding probe to cloud-init. snippet:

```bash
# cloud-init user data snippet
if dmesg | grep -q ENA; then
  echo "ENA_OK" > /var/run/ena_ok
else
  aws ec2 create-tags --resources $(curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id) --tags Key=ami_health,Value=fail
fi
```

liz: who owns the alert and runbook if the canary trips?

kai: sec ok with tags. runbook: pager to infra-oncall, create a short lived capacity incident channel, and rollback to previous module version if automated rollback threshold hit.

maya: action items: 
- maya: push TF branch and PR with module changes and canary variables
- arjun: add cloud-init probe + small smoke harness
- sam: review canary thresholds and approve PR
- liz: prepare runbook and alerting (pager + slack hook)

maya: I'll squash plan and include the terraform graph in PR. pinging @sam for review. :eyes:

sam: on it — will review today. :thumbsup:

terraform-bot: apply queued but gated by manual approval in ci.

maya: also note cost modeling: early sims show 9-11% cost savings on mixed pools if hyst >10% because we avoid frequent degrades to on-demand. i'll add detailed numbers to PR.

liz: sounds good. if the ENA probe false-positive rate is >2% we should tune dmesg pattern to avoid churning.

maya: agreed — will add metrics around probe failures and sample logs.

sam: thanks everyone. merging plan once PR addresses feedback.
